# dlaev2

> Computes the eigendecomposition of a 2-by-2 symmetric matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlaev2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlaev2';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlaev2( a, b, c, rt1, rt2, cs1, sn1 ) → void
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `a` | `number` | in |  |  | (1,1) element of the 2-by-2 matrix |
| `b` | `number` | in |  |  | (1,2) element (also (2,1)) of the 2-by-2 matrix |
| `c` | `number` | in |  |  | (2,2) element of the 2-by-2 matrix |
| `rt1` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the eigenvalue of larger absolute value |
| `rt2` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the eigenvalue of smaller absolute value |
| `cs1` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): `cs1` |
| `sn1` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the vector (CS1, SN1) is a unit right eigenvector for RT1 |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `a`: The (1,1) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `b`: The (1,2) element and the conjugate of the (2,1) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `c`: The (2,2) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `rt1`: The eigenvalue of larger absolute value.
- `rt2`: The eigenvalue of smaller absolute value.
- `sn1`: The vector (`CS1`, `SN1`) is a unit right eigenvector for `RT1`.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlaev2.ndarray( a, b, c, rt1, rt2, cs1, sn1 ) → void
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `a` | `number` | in |  |  | (1,1) element of the 2-by-2 matrix |
| `b` | `number` | in |  |  | (1,2) element (also (2,1)) of the 2-by-2 matrix |
| `c` | `number` | in |  |  | (2,2) element of the 2-by-2 matrix |
| `rt1` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the eigenvalue of larger absolute value |
| `rt2` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the eigenvalue of smaller absolute value |
| `cs1` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): `cs1` |
| `sn1` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the vector (CS1, SN1) is a unit right eigenvector for RT1 |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `a`: The (1,1) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `b`: The (1,2) element and the conjugate of the (2,1) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `c`: The (2,2) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `rt1`: The eigenvalue of larger absolute value.
- `rt2`: The eigenvalue of smaller absolute value.
- `sn1`: The vector (`CS1`, `SN1`) is a unit right eigenvector for `RT1`.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

## Notes

-   `dlaev2()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLAEV2`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlaev2.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import dlaev2 from './../lib/base.js';

// Compute the eigendecomposition of a 2-by-2 symmetric matrix:

//   [ 2.0  1.0 ]

//   [ 1.0  3.0 ]
const rt1 = new Float64Array( 1 );
const rt2 = new Float64Array( 1 );
const cs1 = new Float64Array( 1 );
const sn1 = new Float64Array( 1 );

dlaev2( 2.0, 1.0, 3.0, rt1, rt2, cs1, sn1 );

console.log( 'Eigenvalue of larger absolute value (rt1):', rt1[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'Eigenvalue of smaller absolute value (rt2):', rt2[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'Cosine of rotation (cs1):', cs1[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'Sine of rotation (sn1):', sn1[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLAEV2`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLAEV2 computes the eigendecomposition of a 2-by-2 symmetric matrix

$$
\begin{bmatrix} A & B \\ B & C \end{bmatrix}
$$

On return, `RT1` is the eigenvalue of larger absolute value, `RT2` is the eigenvalue of smaller absolute value, and (`CS1`,`SN1`) is the unit right eigenvector for `RT1`, giving the decomposition

$$
\begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{CS1} & \mathrm{SN1} \\ -\mathrm{SN1} & \mathrm{CS1} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} A & B \\ B & C \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{CS1} & -\mathrm{SN1} \\ \mathrm{SN1} & \mathrm{CS1} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{RT1} & 0 \\ 0 & \mathrm{RT2} \end{bmatrix}
$$

### Further Details

`RT1` is accurate to a few ulps barring over/underflow.

`RT2` may be inaccurate if there is massive cancellation in the determinant $A \, C-B \, B$; higher precision or correctly rounded or correctly truncated arithmetic would be needed to compute `RT2` accurately in all cases.

`CS1` and `SN1` are accurate to a few ulps barring over/underflow.

Overflow is possible only if `RT1` is within a factor of 5 of overflow. Underflow is harmless if the input data is 0 or exceeds

underflow\_threshold / macheps.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
